title: Spontaneous Formation and Rearrangement of Artificial Lipid Nanotube Networks as a Bottom-Up Model for Endoplasmic Reticulum
protocol: Place in a clean 10 mL round-bottom or inverted pear-shaped glass flask: Soy L-α phosphatidyl choline (PC, 69% w/w), 1,2-dioleoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphoethanolamine (DOPE, 30% w/w), and a lipid-conjugated fluorophore of choice [e.g., Texas Red 1,2-dihexadecanoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphoethanolamine triethylammonium salt (TR-DHPE, 1% w/w)] in chloroform; for a total amount of 3000 µg of lipids in 300 µL of chloroform.
Connect the flask to a rotary evaporator.
Position the flask with a tilt of 45°.
Rotate the flask at 24 rpm inside a water bath at 23 °C.
Start reducing the pressure right after initiating rotation by steps of 20 kPa every 2 min until it reaches 20 kPa (150 Torr, 80% vacuum).
Maintain the slow reduction steps as well as the end pressure and rotation velocity to ensure uniform lipid film formation.
After 6 h, stop the rotation and increase the air pressure by steps of 20 kPa every 2 min until reaching 100 kPa.
Remove the flask from the rotary evaporator and add 3 mL of PBS and 30 µL of glycerol.
Gently swirl the flask to dissolve the glycerol.
Use an air-tight glass stopper to seal the flask containing the lipids.
Store the flask in the refrigerator at 4 °C overnight for rehydration and swelling of the lipid films.
Sonicate the lipids with an ultrasonic water bath at room temperature (~21 °C) and at 35 kHz frequency until achieving a uniform, slightly turbid lipid suspension.
Divide the lipid suspension into 100 µL aliquots using 30 microcentrifuge tubes.
Store the lipid suspensions in a freezer at -20 °C.
Set the temperature of the ALD reactor to 200 °C.
Load the glass surfaces into the sample chamber together with a silicon wafer.
Evacuate the loading chamber to 400 Pa and transfer the samples into the main reaction chamber.
Evacuate the main reaction chamber to 200 Pa.
Maintain the reactor temperature at 200 °C for proper deposition.
Equilibrate any temperature fluctuations before initiating the deposition process.
Set chamber pressure higher than reactor pressure to prevent precursor spread outside the chamber.
Start depositing the atomic film.
Pulse trimethyl aluminum exposure for 150 ms, followed by a purge of 1 s.
Expose to H2O for 200 ms, followed by another purge of 1 s.
Repeat the deposition cycle for 100 cycles to achieve 10 nm of Al2O3 on the substrate.
Vent the chamber until its pressure reaches atmospheric pressure.
Remove samples from the reactor once venting is complete.
Store removed samples in air-tight containers at room temperature until use.
Thaw the lipid suspension.
Transfer a 4 µL droplet of lipid suspension onto a clean glass microscope slide/coverslip.
Desiccate the droplet for 20 min.
Rehydrate the lipid film with 1 mL of HEPES buffer for 3 min.
Prepare the observation chamber for buffer exchange by using an automatic pipette.
Fabricate a PDMS frame with dimensions 1.5 x 1.5 x 0.5 cm.
Adhere the PDMS frame onto an Al2O3 deposited coverslip to assemble the observation chamber.
Prepare a KOH solution by mixing 100 g of KOH with 100 mL of isopropanol in a beaker in an ice bath.
Stir the mixture for 10 h or longer until the KOH is completely dissolved using a magnetic stirrer and magnetic stir plate.
Submerge a glass Petri dish into the KOH solution at room temperature and keep it overnight.
Remove the glass dish from the solution the following day.
Immerse the glass dish in a container with deionized water for 5 min.
Rinse the glass dish several times with water.
Place the glass dish inside a drying oven at 80 °C for 1 h.
Briefly blow the surface of the glass dish with a stream of nitrogen to ensure that particles are removed.
Transfer 200 µL of dimethyldichlorosilane with a plastic syringe into a clean plastic container such as a weighting boat.
Store the glass Petri dish together with the silane for 1 h in an evacuated desiccator at low vacuum (approximately 20 kPa).
Wait 15 min before collecting the Petri dish to allow dimethyldichlorosilane vapor to dissipate.
Place a water droplet onto the silanized Petri dish to test surface hydrophobicity.
Mix 10 g of silicone elastomer base with 1 g of silicone elastomer curing agent in a plastic container for 5 min.
Desiccate the mixture to degas at less than 20 kPa until all air bubbles have collapsed.
Pour the degassed mixture into the silanized Petri dish.
Cure the PDMS at 65 °C for 2 h in an oven.
Cool down the Petri dish filled with cured PDMS to room temperature.
Remove the PDMS slab from the Petri dish using a spatula.
Cut the PDMS frame into dimensions of 1.5 cm x 1.5 cm x 0.5 cm using a scalpel.
Bring the smooth side of the PDMS frame into contact with the active side of the surface where the Al2O3 film resides.
Gently apply pressure to push the frame and surface against each other to make them adhere.
Rinse the PDMS frame with isopropanol after each use, followed by rinsing with DI water and blow-drying with nitrogen.
Fill the observation chamber with Ca2+-HEPES buffer immediately after assembly.
Place the chamber onto the confocal microscope stage.
Transfer the rehydrated lipid material into the chamber using a plastic Pasteur pipette.
Wait 10-20 min for vesicles to adhere onto the substrate and spread across the surface.
Slowly remove ambient buffer via an automatic pipette, leaving only a thin film on the bottom.
Proceed with ambient buffer exchange by slowly filling the observation chamber with chelator-HEPES buffer using an automatic pipette.
Acquire images with an inverted laser scanning confocal microscope using a 40X oil immersion objective.
Use a white light laser source to excite Texas Red DHPE at 595 nm.
Collect emission from 605 to 700 nm by using a hybrid photon detector.
